statement: For an N-dimensional multivariate normal random vector x ~ N(μ, Σ) partitioned into x1 (q x 1) and x2 ((N - q) x 1) with mean vector μ = [μ1; μ2] and covariance matrix Σ = [Σ11, Σ12; Σ21, Σ22], the marginal distribution of the subset x1 is multivariate normal: x1 ~ N_q(μ1, Σ11), obtained by dropping the marginalized variables x2 from the mean vector and covariance matrix. The supplied sources genuinely contain no derivation (they contain no steps using completing the square or marginalization integrals, noting only that the result follows from definitions of multivariate normal distributions and linear algebra).

properties.property: To obtain the marginal distribution over a subset of multivariate normal random variables, one only needs to drop the irrelevant variables from the mean vector and covariance matrix.
properties.why: The marginal parameters are directly given by the corresponding subvector μ1 and submatrix Σ11.

properties.property: Any subset of components Xi of a multivariate normal vector has a marginal distribution that is also multivariate normal.
properties.why: Extracting a subset is an affine transformation Y = BX with a selection matrix B consisting of rows of the identity matrix, which preserves multivariate normality with Y ~ N(Bμ, B Σ B^T).

properties.property: Any linear combination Z = b · X of a multivariate normal vector X is univariate Gaussian distributed as Z ~ N(b · μ, b^T Σ b).
properties.why: It is a one-dimensional affine transformation using projection matrix B = b^T.

properties.property: The unconditional marginal distribution of x1 is N_q(μ1, Σ11), whereas knowing that x2 = a yields conditional distribution N(μ1 + Σ12 Σ22^-1 (a - μ2), Σ11 - Σ12 Σ22^-1 Σ21).
properties.why: Conditioning shifts the mean and alters covariance via the Schur complement, whereas marginalization leaves the mean at μ1 and covariance at Σ11 without conditioning on a specific value.

properties.property: If a random vector has a multivariate normal distribution, any two or more of its components that are uncorrelated are independent.
properties.why: Pairwise zero correlation in a joint normal distribution implies pairwise and mutual statistical independence.

assumptions.assumption: The full random vector x must be jointly multivariate normally distributed x ~ N(μ, Σ).
assumptions.breaks_when: The individual variables are marginally normal but not jointly normal (e.g., non-linear dependencies such as Y = X for |X| > c and Y = -X for |X| < c).

assumptions.assumption: The covariance matrix Σ must be a valid symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
assumptions.breaks_when: Σ has negative eigenvalues or is not symmetric.

failure_modes.mode: Assuming joint normality from marginal normalities
failure_modes.signature: Individual variables pass 1D normality tests, but linear combinations or joint subsets fail normality tests.
failure_modes.cause: Marginal normality of separate components is necessary but not sufficient to guarantee that the joint distribution is multivariate normal.

failure_modes.mode: Conflating marginal distribution with conditional distribution
failure_modes.signature: Using marginal variance Σ11 and mean μ1 despite having observed x2 = a.
failure_modes.cause: Failing to apply the Schur complement covariance and mean shift induced by conditioning on observed data.
